newsitem.title: DUBAI: Velayati invites Saudi King to Tehran summit.
newsitem.headline: Velayati invites Saudi King to Tehran summit.

text.p: Iran's Foreign Minister Ali Akbar Velayati said on Sunday he had delivered an invitation to Saudi Arabia's King Fahd to attend an Islamic summit in Tehran.
Velayati, who arrived in Riyadh on Saturday on his first visit to the kingdom since 1993, was speaking at a news conference after meeting the Saudi monarch in the Saudi capital Riyadh.
"I have extended the invitation to the king and delivered a message from the Iranian president," Velayati said.
"King Fahd welcomed the invitation and said he would participate as much as it would be possible for him."

Velayati, on a tour of 10 countries since Sunday, is extending invitations to Moslem heads of states and governments from President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani for a summit of the Moslem world's largest body.
The 51-nation Organisation of the Islamic Conference (OIC), which is based in the Saudi commercial capital Jeddah, is due to hold its four-yearly summit in Tehran in December.
Gulf-based diplomats and analysts consider it highly unlikely that King Fahd would go to Tehran.
But they said the invitation presented the Saudi royal family with a diplomatic dilemma.

The kingdom is home to two of Islam's most sacred shrines in the closed cities of Mecca and Medina. King Fahd styles himself Custodian of the Two Holy Shrines, emphasising his guardianship of the Moslem world's most revered places.
The king, or at the very least his half-brother Crown Prince Abdullah who often deputises for him, would be expected to attend the Moslem world's most important gathering, analysts said.
But the Saudis are less than pleased that Iran is about to take over the leadership of the OIC for the next four years.

"Even if there are not many heads of state in Tehran it would still be called a summit and the Iranians would still become chairman. This prospect is dreaded by the Saudis and their friends in the Gulf," a diplomatic source in the Iranian capital said earlier this week.
